tasks.title: Naked eye observation from real sky with panoramic 360-degrees image
tasks.statement:
Included:
- Panoramic 360-degrees image of the sky at night at an unknown location
- Computer screen
- Keypad to pan around the image
- Coordinates of bright stars

parts.question: Estimate the LST (Local Sidereal Time) at the time the image was taken, rounded to nearest hour

tasks.title: Planet observation with real sky in panoramic 360-degrees image
tasks.statement:
Included:
- A panoramic 360-degrees image of the sky at night at an unknown location
- Computer screen
- Keypad to pan around the image

parts.question: Count the number of planets visible in this image above the horizon and name the constellations they’re in (with IAU designations).

tasks.title: Analemma on another planet
tasks.statement:
Included:
- A generated analemma (position of a Star taken from the surface of a planet with interval separated by mean solar day of the planet over an orbital period around a Star) of a fictitious planet orbiting around a Star.
- Result is graphed on a paper with each major grid representing 5°

parts.question: Find the Obliquity (Axial Tilt) of the planet

tasks.title: Exposure time from a Photograph
tasks.statement:
Included:
- A “Star Trails” image that was taken by a still camera capturing image over a period of time.
- Ruler

parts.question: Estimate an exposure time of a given “Star Trails” image.

tasks.title: Find True North from Moon shadow
tasks.statement:
Included:
- Simulated position of moon shadows of a pole at certain intervals in the span of a day.
- The observer is located in the Southern hemisphere at latitude 27°S.
- The moon’s declination that night is +15°
- Ruler, Compass (drawing tool), Geometry kit

parts.question: Draw an arrow pointing North in the data sheet

tasks.title: Find Latitude from Equatorial Mount
tasks.statement:
Included:
- An Equatorial Mount Telescope that has already been properly aligned to a location in the northern celestial pole.
- Bubble Level.
- Latitude dial on the mount is covered (you may not use it).

parts.question: Without altering the polar alignment, find the observer’s latitude based on a previously polar-aligned equatorial mount.

tasks.title: Precision Polar Alignment with Equatorial Mount
tasks.statement:
Included:
- Equatorial Mount with polar scope (has not been polar aligned)
- Date and Time (GMT, UTC+0) of the time performing the polar alignment
- Diagram of the sky’s position at the time
- A light source to be substituted with Polaris to be used for proper polar alignment (already visible in the polar scope)
- Longitude of observer

Date and Time : 30 Aug 2017 / 23:30
Longitude : 10 0 E

parts.question: Perform a polar alignment on the equatorial mount provided
